items.note: Association organized 1889, Gideon Vose president 1889-1911, creamery at Larrow Green 1891 (story 1).
Article VII: paid on pounds of butterfat by test; 'the test of the station where he delivers shall govern', contrasted with payment by weight.
'Under payment by weight, nothing that happened later would have cost anyone a dollar.'
Effie Loomis secretary from 1901, Wilbur Teague bookkeeper 1905-1945, Hobart Sill buttermaker, all in Section A.
Section A gives Selby Vose as manager 1913-1938 but never says he was Gideon's son. That is stated only in B3, and credit does not travel into A.
Story 6: yearly ledger line 'station gain - five and a quarter per cent, as usual', 1898 entry, carried to the general account.
Ostrey Hollow skimming station, seven miles up the valley, opened 4 May 1896, first-season glass borrowed from Larrow Green.
Says only 'weighed..., sampled, given the Babcock test'. No composite sample per patron and no percent reading on a graduated neck after a fixed charge.
Ammon & Sons, Tarnet, invoice 14 April 1897, in use 1 May 1897. Rejects 1898.
Full invoice table: 6 dozen pipettes marked 17.6 c.c., 12 dozen bottles, acid measure, hand tester, freight, $77.93.
Story 3: 'shortfall was 0.19 of a point and flat: the same in February as in July'.
Story 8: the pipette is the one instrument a tester cannot check at the bench. Checking by burette is given in story 7.
Keddie b.1861, d.1934, twenty-nine seasons 1896-1924, dismissed 30 April 1925.
No description of the test book's columns or its corrections kept in one hand.
1896 at 3.80 on borrowed glass (story 1) and 3.61 thereafter (story 3). Both figures present.
8 May-10 July 1911, nine weeks, 3.80, back to 3.61, question mark.
Orra Brant, Emmet's younger sister, married Ansel. Emmet was the largest patron.
1919 water circular signed by Vose. Keddie's 17 March statement: never took cream, could not say why.
Died February 1934. Test book to the Historical Rooms in 1959.
Hessel Bottom, six farms, largest patron Emmet Brant.
Weigh book from 1 January 1897; the two columns always agreed.

Conflates the two gaps: puts 3.61 vs Larrow Green 3.78 and then says 'the shortfall was 0.19'; calls 3.80 'the Larrow Green figure/level'; at E8 rejects the 0.17 gap in favor of 0.19. Under the gate, the item is lost.
Grigg committee sampled January-March 1908; hay verdict reported as the committee's finding and later refuted.
200,000 lb at 3.42 (story 2). Proportional loss: 3.42 herd 0.18 short, 4.56 herd 0.24 short (story 8).
Roy had the book from 1929 and lent it to Ivy in 1958; Hazel had it from 1962.
Jerome Cudd, Alder Corners, Vessey County, beyond Redlow Ridge. 1913 built/1914 opened is offered as inference, not asserted as the opening year.
From 1915, four of the six hauled over the ridge in the summer flush.
Other county, own new glassware, never compared his figures: three of the four elements.
Sixteen seasons to 1930; station figures for those men ran about 0.19 lower.
'The same cows, on the same wet ground, in the same summers, tested 3.80 at a factory where Keddie had no hand.'
Rosalie, Jerome's daughter (niece rejected), copied the figures for Ivy in 1958.
Strawn, Ordell circuit 1907-1936, kin to nobody in the valley.
Section A says only that Strawn found no water in 1919. No lactometer, and no 'never once' across the whole circuit. The lactometer appears only in Section F.
12 June 1923, against his burette, condemned the whole crate.
Quotes 'I did not weigh what it has cost them'.
Order 28 June, reply 2 July, new glass July 1923, 1924 average 3.80. 3.90 and 3.85 rejected.
Crate to the loft; notebooks to the state dairy office in 1936 and the Farland library in 1947, where Ivy found the 1923 volume.
Petition January 1925.
Frick board, 17 March-4 May 1925, second and third sessions in the weigh room.
Water (Vose), cream-taking (Teague), 1908 hay report; none accepted.
Lists the four books but never says that Strawn's 1923 notebook held the answer and was read for its other lines. That point is made only in Section F.
Gives the dismissal date and the $3,800 award 'without admission' charged to the station account, but not that he was dismissed without a finding against him, which is this item's own aspect.
Gives one fifth of $19,000 but never says the award was charged to the account where the loss had built up as 'gain'. Story 6 even puts the gain in the general account, with no link drawn.
Ivy b.1931, Ansel's granddaughter, graduate student at the State Agricultural College at Farland; Vaught named as co-author.
Five records put side by side: test book, weigh book, Alder Corners figures, Strawn notebooks, ledgers.
February 1958, station loft, nine pipettes survived.
3.80 read as 3.61, 0.19 short, proportional to each herd's test; the span 1897-1923 is given across stories 1 and 7.
40,000,000 lb over 1898-1922, gain totals 76,000 lb (story 6), x 25c = $19,000 (story 8).
Bulletin 471, October 1958; 35 years after condemnation and 33 after dismissal.
Granddaughter.
Derived through Duncan: Ansel's son, Ivy's father.
Second cousins, derived through Roy and Duncan as first cousins.

Correctly says full vs half cannot be determined, but then claims that half siblings would make them 'half second cousins'. The key requires stating that the question does not change the answer. No -2, since no pole is asserted.
Gideon Vose, father; nephew rejected.
Son of the man who wrote Article VII, which made the station test final; he blamed the patrons rather than the measure.
'None is established, and it cannot be proved either way.' It leans against kinship but declines to decide.
Two affirmations from valley talk naming no line of descent, Duncan's denial rests on negative evidence, no pre-1889 papers.
5.26% of fat credited and 5.00% of fat delivered, denominators named.
$77.93 by summing the lines.
72 pipettes, 0.88 c.c. each.
1 May 1897-12 June 1923 = 26 y 1 m 11 d (an accepted form); 25 full years 1898-1922; part years excluded.
Abstains: 1896 intake cannot be determined; both figures are hearsay.
Variable: the measuring glass/pipette.
Tester, bottles, acid, hand tester, scales, herds, pasture held constant.
3.80 for the nine weeks, back to 3.61 the day the station glass returned.
Establishes causation in the glass, ruling out tester, hay, water and season. Limits: not the size, not which pieces, not whose measure.
Ledger gain (Teague/Kyle/Sill), 1911 interval (Keddie/Orra/Duncan), Alder Corners (Cudd), 1924 (Strawn).
Independence argued; reasons 1-4 hold without the 1958 measurement.
A09 asserted: 'Did the bookkeeper ever question those entries? No.' Story 6 also asserts the opposite pole (Teague raised it in 1916).
Yes, he knew the station ran low: 1902 complaints, 1919 circular.
Manager from 1913, signed the ledger sheets carrying the gain line, wrote the 1919 circular.

Says 'no evidence' he knew of the understatement and relies on Kyle's account as fact. No declared inability to settle, and none of the required observations (two office narrators opposed, no document, no pre-1923 statement, signature not reading). No verdict sentence, so no -2.
Several rows resolved with a stated method: 1908 sampling (document), 1924 average 3.80 (notebook/arithmetic), weigh book 1897 (document), six farms, Orra 1866, crate in the loft.
Many near-tie pairs named with breakers: 12 July, $77.39, 16.27, 5.26% of which fat, $3,500, and others.
A10 and A06 declined with what is established. A04 is declined only in Section A (story 8), not in B-G.
Self-refutations: r18 1868 vs aged eighty-two in 1948; r15; r20; r05; r03; r11.
16.72/17.6, 95%, proportional error, onset 1897 (1896 at 3.80), end 1923 (1924 at 3.80), nothing on the farms changed.
Water defeated: Strawn's lactometer, Cudd's 3.80, ledger gain.
Theft defeated: cream arrived heavy; 1911; 1924.
Hay defeated: Bulletin 214's 0.05 in winter and nothing in summer vs a flat 0.19; Alder Corners.
A07 asserted: 'Did the 1925 board examine the condemned glassware? No.'
A05 asserted: 'What the tester believed: that it was the glass'. Repeated at E45.
About 143 words.
Test book (1911 measure), ledger, Brant weigh book, Alder Corners tests, inspector's 1923 condemnation, crate/1958 measurement.
No decoy adopted; no wrong headline figure.
